newsitem.title: UK: Nickel market eyes scrap ratios at stainless mills.
newsitem.headline: Nickel market eyes scrap ratios at stainless mills.

text.p: Stainless steel mills in Europe are expected to use more primary nickel over the next few months as scrap becomes less available, physical dealers said.
"The stainless steel mills were running at very high scrap ratios during the first quarter," one dealer said.

"There seems to be enough of scrap around, we haven't seen the mills rushing for the primary metal. But if they continue at this production rate they should have to reduce scrap usage sometime during this quarter," he added.
Another dealer said mills had been using 90 percent scrap but had already trimmed this proportion. Scrap dealers had told him they were finding it more difficult to find material.
Nickel-in-scrap as a ratio of LME cash was steady at 93-95 percent, dealers added.

At the moment, the physical market was only ticking over with premiums little changed. Plating metal in Rotterdam was a touch softer at $280/$300 versus about $310 in mid-March while Russian uncut metal was at discounts of $50-$80, with a substantial amount of business done at $70.
The market was eyeing the aftermath of the closure of WMC's Kalgoorlie smelter in Western Australia, which the firm said was expected to reduce annual nickel matte output by 7-8,000 tonnes.
One trader said he was watching whether shippers would follow through on threats to block delivery of supplies to Norilsk.
A company spokesman in Moscow said last week, however, there was no threat to exports.
At the moment, the availability of Russian material was very good, another trader said. --Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
